title: It had made $0 in revenue.
description:
Facebook's cash offer to buy Snapchat outright, November 2013; rejected.

It had made $0 in revenue. Evan Spiegel turned down the offer anyway, betting on growth.

A rumoured $4 billion Google offer is often repeated as fact. It traces to a single journalist's tweet, never confirmed by Google or a named primary source; Forbes flagged the $3B-vs-$4B confusion as unresolved at the time.

Usage was still climbing fast. Snapchat's daily photos and messages grew from 200 million to 350 million between June and September 2013 alone.

Explained the decision on the Diary of a CEO podcast: 'we decided that we would rather go it alone.'

Sources:
- https://www.csmonitor.com/Technology/Horizons/2013/1116/Why-did-Snapchat-s-23-year-old-CEO-reject-a-3-billion-buyout-offer - established the $3 billion all-cash Facebook offer (via WSJ), that Snapchat had no revenue at the time, and that daily photo/message volume rose from 200 million to 350 million between June and September 2013.
- https://www.forbes.com/sites/davidwismer/2013/11/17/snapchat-how-to-make-3-billion-or-was-it-4-billion-disappear-and-other-quotes-of-the-week/ - established that the $3 billion Facebook figure is solidly reported while a separate $4 billion Google offer is only a 'latest rumour', and explicitly flagged the two figures as often confused.
- https://www.shellypalmer.com/2013/11/google-snapchat/ - traced the '$4 billion Google offer' claim to a single journalist's tweet, never confirmed by Google or a named primary source.
- https://www.uniladtech.com/social-media/snapchat/snapchat-ceo-evan-spiegel-3billion-mark-zuckerberg-622036-20250325 - reported Evan Spiegel's own 2025 account on the Diary of a CEO podcast, quoting him directly: 'we decided that we would rather go it alone.'
- https://techcrunch.com/2017/03/01/snap-values-itself-at-nearly-24b-with-its-ipo-pricing - established Snap Inc.'s IPO pricing at $17 a share, valuing the company at nearly $24 billion in March 2017.
